BETA
Local stdio resource discovery and manifest tools are the supported core boundary. Remote HTTP/SSE, recommendations and advanced mutation workflows are Beta; this public Site does not host an MCP process.
← Back to Documentation
Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Connect a local MCP client to search resources, read manifests and source, compose projects, validate or audit manifests, and generate export files.

Configuration

The MCP server is a private workspace package, not an npm download. Clone Tessellate locally, then point your agent at that checkout:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tessellate": {
      "command": "pnpm",
      "args": ["--dir", "C:\\path\\to\\Tessellate", "exec", "tsx", "packages/mcp/src/index.ts"]
    }
  }
}

Use the absolute path to your checkout. Keep the local catalogue and resource source in that checkout; stdio is the supported local transport.

Available MCP Tools
search_resources: Searches the validated catalogue by query and category.
get_resource: Retrieves the complete validated ResourceManifest for a given component slug.
get_resource_code: Reads the resource source from the local checkout. A missing local file returns an explicit tool error.
recommend_resources BETA: Ranks candidates by lexical token overlap. It does not perform semantic ranking or guarantee a fit.
find_alternatives BETA: Lists same-type resources with a shared category. These candidates are not guaranteed drop-in replacements.
compose_screen and compose_product BETA: Call the shared deterministic product pipeline; a fixed seed reproduces a direction.
validate_project, mutate_screen_ast, and export_project_code BETA: Validate manifests, apply supported atomic edits, and generate source files. Export generation does not install or build the result.
audit_project and audit_project_accessibility BETA: Manifest heuristics only; neither tool certifies rendered WCAG conformance.
get_resource_metadata, get_design_dna, and list_design_directions: Return canonical metadata, preset IDs, and the stable A/B/C composition approaches.

The optional HTTP/SSE helper is Beta, has no authentication, and binds to loopback by default. Do not expose it through a tunnel or network interface. Browser origins require an explicit allowlist.
